reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Petition amendments and supplemental pre-hearing petitions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1947 V. I p. 452 § 4, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971). Prevents voiding a petition with requisite signatures for alleged defects, allows county commission-permitted amendments to conform to facts, and allows filing similar/duplicate pre-hearing petitions revising boundaries, name, or first-board recommendations to be treated as one petition.

headings.title: Petition filing fee for publication notices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers the $100 filing fee submitted with the petition(s) for county commission use to pay hearing and question-submission publication notices.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1947 V. I p. 452 § 4, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971) and verified all fingerprints. Checked non-voiding of defective petitions with requisite signatures, permissive county commission amendments, consolidated pre-hearing similar/duplicate petitions, and the $100 filing fee for hearing and submission publication notices; both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Organization order, boundaries, and corporate status pending election
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1947 V. I p. 452 § 7, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971). Covers entering a county commission record order declaring a district organized upon a compliant section 235.030 petition and no sustained protesting petition, defining/changing boundaries, naming the district, and conferring political-subdivision/corporate status subject to the section's ratification election. Retains verbatim duplicated source phrasing ("making such changes in the boundaries thereof, making such changes in the boundary line") without silent editing.

headings.title: Voter ratification requirement for final incorporation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Makes the incorporation order non-final until submitted to district voters on county commission order and approved by a majority of voters voting on the question.

headings.title: Ballot form for district incorporation question
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (including indented ballot block) and history note. Sets the substantial ballot language for incorporating a street light maintenance district.

headings.title: Commission orders following favorable or unfavorable vote
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers county commission entry of a further order declaring incorporation final and conclusive upon a favorable majority vote, or void and of no effect if a majority does not vote in favor.

headings.title: Designation and staggered terms of first board
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Covers county commission designation of the first board of directors (upon final incorporation order) from voters named in filed petitions, with staggered terms until the first biennial election, two years after, and four years after.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all five subsections (including indented ballot block in subsection 3) and history note (L. 1947 V. I p. 452 § 7, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971) and verified all fingerprints. Checked section 235.030 hearing/organization order (retaining duplicated boundary-change source phrasing verbatim), ratification election condition, ballot form, final versus void orders, and first-board designation with staggered biennial terms; all five drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Board election timing, six-year term, and nominations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1947 V. I p. 452 § 14, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971). Covers electing one board member for a six-year term at the general election in the year after the first full calendar year following district organization and at general elections thereafter, and permissive filing of nominations with the board secretary.

headings.title: Nonpartisan ballot, plurality election, and member qualification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers election on a separate nonpartisan ballot, election of the candidate receiving the most votes, and qualifying in the same manner as first-board members.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1947 V. I p. 452 § 14, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971) and verified all fingerprints. Checked general-election timing after first full calendar year, six-year terms, permissive board-secretary nominations, separate nonpartisan ballot, plurality election, and qualification matching first-board members; both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Voter approval requirement for tax levy increases
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1978 H.B. 1624 § 2, Effective 5-31-78). Requires majority voter approval before a street light maintenance district board may increase the district's current tax levy.

headings.title: Submitting increase propositions and section 115.123 timing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and section notes. Covers permissive submission of a tax levy increase proposition by the board of directors or upon petition of 500 registered district voters, scheduled at the next election permitted by section 115.123.

headings.title: Separate ballot form for levy increase
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (including ballot block and voter marking instructions) and section notes. Sets the separate ballot wording for submitting a district tax levy increase.

headings.title: Effect of voter approval or rejection of increase
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and section notes. Covers raising the levy to the voter-approved level upon a favorable majority vote and retaining any previously authorized levy if a majority does not vote in favor.

headings.title: Maximum levy cap under section 235.170
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and section notes. Prohibits any street light maintenance district from fixing a levy rate exceeding the maximum tax levy authorized by section 235.170.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all five subsections (including ballot block and voter instructions in subsection 3) and history/effective-date notes (L. 1978 H.B. 1624 § 2, Effective 5-31-78) and verified all fingerprints. Checked majority voter-approval requirement, board or 500-voter petition submission at section 115.123 elections, separate ballot wording, approval/rejection effects, and section 235.170 maximum levy cap; all five drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Boundary change authority and preserved rights and obligations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1947 V. I p. 452 § 21, A.L. 1967 p. 353, A.L. 2007 S.B. 22). Authorizes changing district boundaries under this section and section 235.220 while specifying that boundary changes do not impair organization, property rights, privileges, contracts, obligations, liens, or charges (retaining source wording "or shall it affect or impair" verbatim). Independent review revised title from 'Boundary change authority and preservation of obligations' because subsection 1 preserves organization, property rights, and other rights/privileges alongside contracts, obligations, liens, and charges.

headings.title: Annexation petitions, hearings, and dual-area election orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers petitions by owners of at least 10% of parcels in contiguous unincorporated territory (outside any municipality or other street light maintenance district), filing with the county clerk addressed to the county commission, prompt hearing, and ordering submission to voters in both the proposed area and the district at a municipal, primary, or general election if compliant.

headings.title: Ballot form for territory annexation question
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (including ballot block and marking instructions) and history note. Sets the substantial ballot form for submitting a street light maintenance district annexation question.

headings.title: Annexation orders, filing, rejection, and twelve-month resubmission bar
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers commission annexation order and altered boundary description upon separate majorities in both the district and proposed area, filing with the county recorder (noting source wording "filed within the county recorder"), non-annexation if either majority fails, and a 12-month waiting period before resubmission.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections (including ballot block and instructions in subsection 3) and history note (through A.L. 2007 S.B. 22) and verified all fingerprints. Checked section 235.220 cross-reference and preservation of organization, rights, privileges, and obligations (retaining source phrasing 'or shall it affect or impair'), 10%-parcel contiguous unincorporated annexation petitions and dual-area election orders, ballot form, and annexation orders/recording (retaining 'filed within the county recorder')/12-month resubmission bar. Revised subsection 1 to 'Boundary change authority and preserved rights and obligations'; retained subsections 2-4.

headings.title: Property owner petitions for exclusion from district
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1947 V. I p. 452 § 22). Covers permissive filing with the board by owner(s) of real or personal property inside district boundaries of a petition describing property sought to be excluded.

headings.title: Published notice of exclusion petition and objections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers board secretary's publication of notice in the property's county stating petitioners, property description, and prayer, and notifying interested persons to appear at the board office to show cause in writing against granting the petition.

headings.title: Board hearing, written objections, and petitioner assent
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers board hearing of the petition and written show-cause objections at the noticed or adjourned time, and treating petition filing as petitioners' assent to exclusion of all or part of the described property.

headings.title: Board denial or order excluding property
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers mandatory board denial if exclusion is deemed not in the district's best interests, versus permissive board order excluding all or part of the property if deemed in the district's best interest.

headings.title: Filing board order, commission exclusion order, and recording
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Covers filing a certified board allowance order with the county clerk, exclusion taking effect upon county commission order, and filing copies of both orders with the recorder.

headings.title: Standard for county commission review of board order
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Requires the county commission to enter an exclusion order matching the board's order unless it finds the board's order was unauthorized by law or unsupported by competent and substantial evidence.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all six subsections and history note (L. 1947 V. I p. 452 § 22) and verified all fingerprints. Checked property-owner exclusion petitions for real or personal property, published notice, board hearing/written objections and petitioner assent, mandatory denial versus permissive exclusion order, certified clerk/commission/recorder filings, and county commission review standard (authorized by law and supported by competent and substantial evidence); all six drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Dissolution petitions, evidentiary hearing, and submission authority
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1947 V. I p. 452 § 25, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971). Covers filing a petition of at least 100 district voters with the county commission alleging continued operation is inimicable to inhabitants' best interests and dissolution serves public welfare and safety, and county commission authority after hearing evidence to order voter submission.

headings.title: Ballot form for district dissolution question
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including indented ballot block) and history note. Sets the substantial ballot wording for submitting dissolution of a street light maintenance district.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections (including indented ballot block in subsection 2) and history note (L. 1947 V. I p. 452 § 25, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971) and verified all fingerprints. Checked 100-voter dissolution petitions alleging continued operation is inimicable to inhabitants' best interests and dissolution serves public welfare/safety, evidentiary hearing before submission authority, and substantial ballot wording; both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Dissolution election order, timing, and certified returns
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history note (L. 1947 V. I p. 452 § 26, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971), and Revisor footnote (*Word "and" appears here in original rolls.). Covers county commission order submitting dissolution upon finding it in inhabitants' best interest, restricting submission to a general election at which a board member is elected, and certifying returns to the commission (noting both the Revisor asterisk footnote and the archived source's verb-less final clause "Returns of the submission of the question certified to the commission.").

headings.title: Final dissolution order and winding-up limitations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and section notes. Covers entering a final dissolution order upon a favorable majority vote with a mandatory proviso continuing the district solely to pay lawful outstanding obligations and dispose of property, barring new costs or obligations except as necessary for prior liabilities or winding up.

headings.title: Dismissal of petition and continued operation after rejection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and section notes. Covers entering a final order declaring an unfavorable result and dismissing the dissolution petition if a majority does not vote in favor, with the district continuing to operate as though no petition had been filed.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections, history note (L. 1947 V. I p. 452 § 26, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971), and Revisor footnote (*Word 'and' appears here in original rolls.), and verified all fingerprints. Checked dissolution election order restricted to general elections electing a board member, verified both the Revisor asterisk footnote and verb-less final clause ('Returns of the submission of the question certified to the commission.') without silent correction, and checked final dissolution/winding-up proviso and dismissal/continued operation upon rejection; all three drafted titles retained.
